claims.text: A controlled aging heat treatment can induce nanoscale precipitates in a magnetic high-entropy alloy.
The initial as-cast or solutionized alloy is homogeneous and contains minimal or no nanoscale precipitates.
The nanoscale precipitates produced by aging act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Pinning by the precipitates inhibits magnetic domain-wall motion.
Inhibited domain-wall motion increases resistance to demagnetization.
The increased resistance to demagnetization raises the coercive field.
Aged samples will exhibit a measurable increase in coercive field relative to matched unaged samples.
The coercivity increase depends on the precipitates having an optimal size, distribution, and volume fraction.
Overly large or too few precipitates may fail to increase coercivity.
Valid comparison requires identically homogenized samples and constant magnetic-test temperature and field-ramping speed.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the effect should hold only when suitable precipitates form, whereas the falsification rule treats failure to observe the expected precipitates as grounds for falsification. Failure to create the mediator is a failed intervention or manipulation check, not a decisive test of the conditional mechanism.
